inputOutput.title: Inputs and output controls
inputOutput.description: This entry locks the generation mode to images while leaving the supported image settings available in the composer.

items.title: Required input
items.description: A text prompt. Reference images are optional and change the task toward guided generation or editing.

items.title: Image controls
items.description: Choose a supported aspect ratio, 1K, 2K, or 4K resolution, and low, medium, or high quality.

items.title: Continuation
items.description: The first request opens a chat session so you can ask for revisions instead of restarting the task.

workflow.title: How the image workflow works
workflow.description: The tool prepares a focused first turn and hands it to the existing agent runtime.

items.title: 1. Write the visual brief
items.description: Name the main subject and add the details that affect the result: setting, composition, light, material, mood, and intended use.

items.title: 2. Choose image settings
items.description: Select the aspect ratio, resolution, and quality that fit the destination before you submit.

items.title: 3. Continue in chat
items.description: After the first generation starts, use the same session to request focused changes or create another direction.

promptGuide.title: Write prompts that are easier to direct
promptGuide.description: A useful prompt is specific about the visual decision without stuffing every possible adjective into one sentence.

items.title: Lead with the subject and purpose
items.description: State what must appear and where the image will be used before adding stylistic language.

items.title: Describe composition and light
items.description: Camera distance, point of view, negative space, and lighting direction usually provide more control than generic quality words.

items.title: Make constraints explicit
items.description: Call out important exclusions, exact text, required colors, or layout space, then inspect the result and refine only what missed.

limitations.title: What to review before using an output
limitations.description: Image generation is probabilistic. Treat the result as material to inspect, not as a guaranteed reconstruction of the prompt.
items: Fine text, small repeated objects, hands, reflections, and precise spatial relationships may need another pass.
The same prompt can produce different compositions across runs; save the useful result before exploring a new direction.
Uploading a reference does not guarantee pixel-level preservation. Use the dedicated editing workflow when the source image must guide the result.
Generation consumes credits according to the selected image settings; the server recalculates the cost rather than trusting the browser.

items.question: Do I need to upload an image?
items.answer: No. A text prompt is enough for this tool. An optional reference image changes the request toward guided generation or editing.

items.question: Which image settings can I choose?
items.answer: The current image runtime exposes supported aspect ratios, 1K, 2K, and 4K resolution, plus low, medium, and high quality choices.

items.question: Can I revise the image after the first result?
items.answer: Yes. The request opens a chat session, so you can describe the change you want and continue with the existing context.

items.question: Will the same prompt always create the same image?
items.answer: No. Generated images can vary between runs. Use specific composition and lighting instructions, then refine the parts that matter.
